headline: The Trinity reports capability-driven harness evolution across multimodal agent benchmarks
summary: The Trinity paper proposes recursive evolution of tool-using agent harnesses by grouping tasks around shared capability requirements, generating simplified training worlds, and selectively inheriting validated modules while keeping the foundation model fixed. In the current arXiv v2 paper, the authors report mean performance gains of 34 points across 28 training benchmarks and 26 points across 18 unseen benchmarks, including two physical-robot tasks. The results are author-reported; the official code repository was released on 30 October, but this activation did not run or independently reproduce it. The paper itself notes variable benchmark-discovery coverage and limits its present contribution to harness-level self-improvement.
